math.approach: On 2 1/4 + 3 1/4 the digits you wrote were 5 and 2/4, and that is the right answer. They both went into the top of the fraction, though, with the box in front left empty, so it came out as 52/4. On 5 5/12 − 2 2/12 the front box was left empty again. The adding and the subtracting are not what is going wrong here — it is where the whole number lands. The whole number gets its own box, in front, on its own.
math.note: On 5/6 = ?/12, you put 60 on top. Look at what happened underneath: 6 became 12, which is doubling. So the top doubles too — 5 becomes 10, giving 10/12. Whatever you do to the bottom, do exactly the same to the top. Multiplying the top by the new bottom is what gives 60.

focus: writing a mixed number: whole number in its own box, then the fraction
equivalent fractions: do the same to the top as you did to the bottom
reading to the last word: "how much older" needs a take-away after the times

tips.q: Ella is 6 years old. Leo is 3 times as old. How much older is Leo?
tips.note: Your 18 is not a slip — 3 × 6 = 18 is exactly right, and that is Leo's age. The question asks how much older, which is one more step: 18 − 6 = 12. You did the same thing on the Aisha and Zoe one, so it is the last few words of the question to watch, not your times tables.

tips.q: Aisha is 8 years old. Zoe is 3 times as old. How much older is Zoe?
tips.note: Same as the Ella and Leo one: 3 × 8 = 24 is Zoe's age and it is right. "How much older" wants the gap between them, 24 − 8 = 16. Two in a row today, so try reading the question again after you have your first answer.

You divided here, and you divided on the last one of these too. The empty box is the big number — it is the thing being shared out — so it has to be bigger than 32, not smaller. When you see a box before the ÷ sign, multiply.

Your answer here was right. Five and two quarters is exactly it — both digits just went into the top box together, so the app read it as 52/4. Put the 5 in the box in front, on its own, and this one is yours.
